summary: Who is put in service as a game starts, what an order of battle's leader does, and the choice of a leader for a unit, with its eligibility and command size.

addresses.name: CCountry::ActivateRankedLeaders
addresses.comment: **Who is in service as a new game starts**: every leader of country->leaders (+0xE10) whose rank (+0x6C) is not 0 is appended to active_leaders (+0xE00, a CList: last +0xE04, count +0xE08), in the leaders' order. Its one caller is CInGameIdler::Enter at 0x25B276, only where the session was not loaded from a save. The rank is what the leader's history has made it by the start date. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C of 0x4DDCD0; bare `ret`. Checked: the start save's 101 active_leaders lists are the history's leaders with a rank, in this order.

addresses.name: CCountry::AddActiveLeader
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CCountry::AddActiveLeader(CCountry* country@stack:4, CLeader* leader@stack:8, bool record@stack:12)
addresses.comment: Appends a leader to active_leaders (+0xE00) and, with the flag set, files a CLeaderChange dated now (CCurrentGameState->tick) in the country's history at +0xCCC through its slot 6. Callers: leader creation at 0x1D6E6A and 0x1EF1B2, neither read. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C of 0x4DDB80; `ret 0xC`.

addresses.name: CCountry::RemoveActiveLeader
addresses.comment: Finds the leader in active_leaders (+0xE00) and unlinks the node with CList_RemoveNode. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x4DDCA0..0x4DDCC3: `lea esi,[eax+0xe00]`, the walk comparing [node] with edx, bare `ret`.

addresses.name: CUnit::AssignBestLeader
addresses.comment: **The choice of a leader for a unit.** Over the unit's country's active_leaders: skips one with a unit (+0x40) or that CUnit::MayTakeLeader(unit, him, 1) refuses; scores (skill + 1) * 1000, a hundredth of that for a fleet or an air unit with more brigades (+0x40) than CLeader::CommandSize, plus for every effect of every trait a set amount where its kind suits the unit's own definition (byte table 0x1CD8FC over kind - 3, arms at 0x1CD8C4): defence_modifier 10000 under max_speed 3.000; offence_modifier and combat_move_speed 10000 over 4.000 or with base_ca_bonus over 50; river, fort and amphibious attack 20000 for a positive adjuster; combined_arms_bonus 50000 for any base_ca_bonus; submarine_attack 20000 where the first brigade is a submarine; defender_softness 5000 for soft over hard attack; strategic_attack and naval_attack 10000 over air attack; tactical_attack 10000 for soft plus hard over air; paradrop_mission 50000 off the definition's can_paradrop byte, which nothing sets. The effect's figure is never read. Strictly greater wins, from 0, so the first of equals keeps it; then CUnit::SetLeader(unit, him, 0, 0). Nine callers: CInGameIdler::Enter for every leaderless unit of a new game (not gated), and DeployAt, JoinUnit, CCreateHigherCommand::Execute and others gated by CCountry +0x74B. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x5CD5B0..0x5CD8C1 and the decompiled C; the jump table decoded from the image. Reproduces all 1555 unit leaders of the start save that the files share with it.

addresses.name: CLeader::CanCommand
addresses.signature: bool __stdcall CLeader::CanCommand(CLeader* leader@EAX, CUnit* unit@EDI, bool onlyFree@stack:4) @AL
addresses.comment: No for a leader of rank 0, for a land unit and a leader whose type (+0x68) is not 0, a naval one and type not 1, an air one and type not 2; with the flag, no where he has a unit (+0x40) that is not this one. Otherwise yes. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x5BFB30..0x5BFB91, `ret 4`; the unit's slots 15, 16 and 17 are IsLand, IsNaval, IsAir.

addresses.name: CUnit::MayTakeLeader
addresses.signature: bool __stdcall CUnit::MayTakeLeader(CUnit* unit@ECX, CLeader* leader@ESI, bool onlyFree@AL) @AL
addresses.comment: CLeader::CanCommand, and for a land unit an exact rank by oob_level (+0x1F4): a division 1 and CUnit::GetCounterSize not 0 - more than one brigade - a corps 2, an army 3, an army group and a theatre 4. A fleet or an air unit takes any rank. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x5BFBA0..: `push edi; push eax; mov edi,ecx; mov eax,esi; call 0x5BFB30`, bare `ret`; the level arms from the decompiled C.

addresses.name: CLeader::CommandSize
addresses.comment: How many ships or wings a leader's rank commands: for a naval unit NAVAL_RANK_2, _3 or _4 by rank (+0x6C) and NAVAL_RANK_1 for any other, for an air unit AIR_RANK_1 to _4 the same way, each over 1000; 0 for a land unit. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 7.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C of 0x5800A0; bare `ret`; the defines by name off CDefinesMilitary.

addresses.name: CUnit::LeaderCommandsEnough
addresses.comment: The fleet and air arm of CUnit::LeaderHasRankForCommand: yes for a land unit, else yes where CLeader::CommandSize(leader, unit) is at least the unit's brigade count (+0x40). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 7.

addresses.name: AI_ReassignLeaders
addresses.comment: The AI's reshuffle of a country's leaders, called once from ProcessAI at 0x489AD6: scores every unit of the country named at ai +0x20 into CUnit +0x2C0 (0x499500), weighs each free active leader against the one in place by those scores, and posts a CAssignLeaderCommand(unit, leader, 1) for each improvement, clearing ai +0xA4. Read for its shape; 0x499500 and when ProcessAI calls it were not read. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 8.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C of 0x898EF0; `ret 4`. Likely, not confirmed, as to what the scores mean - hence inferred.

addresses.name: CUnit::SetLeader
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CUnit::SetLeader(CUnit* this, CLeader* leader, bool resetTraitHours, bool organisationHit)
addresses.comment: **Puts a leader on a unit, or takes one off by being given `CLeader::null()`.** `this` in ECX, three stack arguments, `ret 0xc`. Where the new leader differs: the old one's unit is set to null and his unit cleared; whatever the new one commanded is set to null and his unit becomes this; **resetTraitHours** zeroes his CTraitGainTracker's duration and sets current to -1, throwing away banked battle hours; **organisationHit** multiplies every brigade's organisation by NEW_LEADER_ORG_HIT / 1000 (not below 0) unless a custom game setting's first byte is set. Then the counter's name is redone - `???` under intelligence 5, else the leader's name, else empty - unless the game setting at +0xE9. The start and CUnit::AssignBestLeader pass (0, 0); CAssignLeaderCommand::Execute (1, 1). 23 callers. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 9.
addresses.evidence: Read whole from the decompiled C of 0x5BFC10.
addresses.revises: Said the two trailing ints were flags whose meaning was not established; they are named and typed now.

addresses.name: CUnit::LeaderHasRankForCommand
addresses.comment: **The gate on BM_LEADER_BONUS**, and what the unit panel writes a leader's name in red for. `this` in EAX, a jump table on oob_level (+0x1F4) against the leader's **rank** (+0x6C): 0 and 1 rank above 2, 2 above 1, 3 above 0, 4 and 7 yes, 5 and 6 - fleet and air - CUnit::LeaderCommandsEnough (0x1CD920). Looser than the exact rank CUnit::MayTakeLeader asks when a leader is chosen. Called at 0x16AA22 and inlined in the naval, air and target slot 19s. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 7.
addresses.evidence: Read whole from the decompiled C of 0x5CD960, with 0x5CD920.
addresses.revises: Promoted from likely to confirmed; the deferred arm is read.

addresses.name: CLeader::PostLoad
addresses.comment: CLeader slot 5. Creates the CTraitGainTracker at +0xC4 if the save had none and Inits it; raises current_experience to SKILL_THRESHOLDS[skill-1] << 15 if it is below; falls back to starting_experience (+0xCC) when the experience is zero; then raises skill while current_experience clears SKILL_THRESHOLDS[skill]. It never lowers skill or experience, so the save's skill is a floor rather than the value. The floor of skill s is the int at VA 0x170AEE0 + 4s - 0, 1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, 12000, 18000, 25000, 33000, 43000, 60000, 100000000 - and skill is raised only while the experience is **strictly above** the next (`jle` out on equal). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 9.
addresses.evidence: The table read out of the image; the comparison off the decompiled C of 0x57FF60.
addresses.revises: Adds the floor table and that the raise wants strictly more.

addresses.name: CUnitDeployment::DeployAt
addresses.no_signature: read for its first two calls only; its `ret` was not reached
addresses.comment: Slot 9: puts the deployment's unit (+0x38) on the map. It adds the unit to its country's list (0x4E06F0, the country from +0x30/+0x34) and calls CUnit::EnterProvince with its one stack argument; what follows builds a message ('UNIT') for the player and was not read. Then, where the country's auto_assign_leaders (+0x74B) is set, CUnit::AssignBestLeader on the unit (0x57DD73). Called by CDeployUnitCommand::Execute and by JoinUnit. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 8.
addresses.revises: Adds the leader it gives a placed unit.

addresses.name: CUnitDeployment::JoinUnit
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CUnitDeployment::JoinUnit(CUnitDeployment* this, CCountry* country, CUnit* target, bool findAnother)
addresses.comment: **Puts a finished unit with one already in the field.** The place is the target's province, or - where the deployment may not be placed there - the nearest province of the capital's area where it may (its ports for a fleet, its air bases for an air unit); none, and nothing happens. The unit is placed (slot 9), the deployment unlinked from the country's list and freed, and then: **a unit of exactly one brigade, of the same service as the target, has that brigade moved into the target** (RemoveRegimentFromUnit, AddRegimentToUnit), a TRANSFEREDSUBUNIT message is raised for the player, the target is given CUnit::AssignBestLeader where it has no leader and the country's auto_assign_leaders is set - while the emptied unit still holds the leader DeployAt gave it - and only then is the emptied unit removed from the game; any other unit is put under the target (0x5B9760). With the flag set the target is first swapped by one of two AI helpers, not read. Called by CDeployUnitCommand::Execute. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 8.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C of 0x5067D0: the call at 0x507024 comes before CGameState::RemoveUnit at the end of the merge path.
addresses.revises: Adds the leader the target is given, and its order against the removal.

addresses.name: CUnit::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CUnit::LoadKey(CUnit* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment:
**The whole of what an order of battle block accepts** - a `division`, `corps`, `army`, `navy`, `air` or `theatre` - 40 keys in one switch of 4658 bytes. Seven open a child unit (`theatre`, `armygroup`, `army`, `corps`, `division`, `navy`, `air`), three say what the unit is made of (`regiment`, `ship`, `wing`, all reaching CSubUnit::LoadKey), four are identity (`id`, `name`, `location`, `leader`) and the rest is state a save carries: `path`, `track`, `previous`, `movement_progress`, `retreat`, `possible_retreat`, `disengage`, `arrow_state`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `was_paradropped`, `supplies`, `fuel`, `dig_in`, `attack_delay`, `combat_hours`, `can_upgrade`, `can_reinforce`, `is_reserve`, `is_prioritized`, `plan`, `expeditionary_owner`, `expeditionary_date`, `aggression_enabled`, `aggression_setting`, `country_intel`. The loader cannot tell an OOB file from a save - it is the same switch - so every one of them is legal in `history/units`.

**The keyword does not pick the class, the parent does**: CNavy::LoadKey and CAir::LoadKey take the five child-unit keywords back and send all five to one handler that still builds a CArmy. Reached from RTTI, not from the first vftable: CArmy keeps CPersistent at object offset 8, so slot 4 of its primary table is a per-unit update and not this. **`leader`** (token 0x268): a plain number is looked up as the persistent {id, type 0x25} across the whole game and put on with CUnit::SetLeader(leader, 0, 0) - no check of his country, rank or kind; a save's {id type} block goes through ParseObjectReference to the same setter. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 3.

struct_fields.name: auto_assign_leaders
struct_fields.comment: Whether a unit placed, joined or made a headquarters is given CUnit::AssignBestLeader. CCountry::SaveContents writes this byte under the key auto_assign_leaders (`movzx eax, byte [edi+0x74B]; mov ecx, 0x5A5; call SaveWriteBool` at 0xD12B6), so the name is read, not inferred. The start's own assignment does not ask it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 8.

struct_fields.name: ai_leader_fit
struct_fields.comment: What AI_ReassignLeaders makes of how well the unit's leader suits it: 0 with no leader, else 0x499500's answer. Read for its shape only. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 8.
struct_fields.evidence: Written in the first loop of 0x898EF0.

slots_noted: None of the new functions sits in a virtual table (vtable.py --holding).
notes: Nothing here was watched in a running game.
Checked against the start save by OpenHOI3's SaveCheck: 101 of 101 countries' active leaders, 1555 of 1555 unit leaders.
